title: Added disector that enhances the RTPS protocol with additional information
description:
[RTI Connext DDS](https://www.rti.com/products) will be able to save sent/received RTPS traffic into a .pcap capture file.

It uses and extends the already existing [RTPS dissector](https://wiki.wireshark.org/Protocols/rtps) to include additional information provided by Connext DDS.

This additional information can be transport-related but also application-level. For example, thanks to the dissector the user is able to analyze decrypted data saved by Connext.

The dissector protocol is not standardized as of today, but the goal is to allow other vendors to use them in their products.

Hi Alexis,

The reason for not including the changes in `packet-rtps.h` is that this file already contains some static variables (e.g. `hf_rtps_dissection_byte`) that I am not using.

As a consequence, if I include `packet-rtps.h` inside `packet-rtps-virtual-transport.c` or `packet-rtps-processed.c` the compiler complains because they are defined but not used.

I actually started the dissector with a previous version of `packet-rtps.h` and had everything there but recent changes added those static, and that is why I created the separate `packet-rtps-common.h`.

Shall I mark this thread as resolved? Or is there anything else I could do about it?

commits_data.title: RTPS-VT: New dissector to enhance the RTPS protocol
commits_data.message:
RTPS-VT: New dissector to enhance the RTPS protocol

Added dissectors for RTPS Virtual Transport and RTPS Processed Protocols

RTI Connext DDS can capture RTPS-related traffic by using the Network Capture
Utility. The generated .pcap capture files will follow these protocols,
establishing a format for how information must be saved, and then
parsed. This will improve debuggability by including additional information
obtained from within Connext DDS.

RTPS-VT parses the information related to the transport. It then, calls
the RTPS-PROC dissector, which handles the rest: calling the RTPS
dissector when needed, and parsing additional information such as the
one related to security.
